q: In MCP specification revision 2026-07-28, what replaced the initialize/notifications-initialized handshake for conveying protocol version and client capabilities?
note: The handshake is gone; every request carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and clientCapabilities in _meta.

q: What happened to the Mcp-Session-Id header in MCP revision 2026-07-28, and how does a server keep state that spans multiple calls now?
note: Sessions are removed; state travels as explicit server-minted handles in ordinary tool arguments.

q: What JSON-RPC error code does a 2026-07-28 MCP server return for a resource that is not found, and which older code must it no longer emit?
note: Changed to align with JSON-RPC Invalid Params; -32002 is retired but accepted from older servers.

q: Which error code and name does an MCP server use when an Mcp-Name header does not match the request body value?
note: 400 Bad Request + HeaderMismatch, renumbered from -32001.

q: What error does an MCP server return for a protocol version it does not implement, and what does its data field list so the client can retry?
note: data.supported lists versions; client retries with a mutual one.

q: In MCP 2026-07-28, how does a server deliver an elicitation/create or sampling/createMessage request to the client, given that server-initiated JSON-RPC requests are no longer allowed?
note: MRTR: the server returns resultType input_required with an inputRequests map; the client retries with inputResponses.

q: What must an MCP client do with the requestState string it receives in an InputRequiredResult?
note: Echo it back exactly on retry; it is opaque and must never be inspected or modified.

q: Which three client request methods are the only ones allowed to receive an input_required result in MCP 2026-07-28?
note: Servers MUST NOT send InputRequiredResult on any other request.

q: Which single method replaced resources/subscribe, resources/unsubscribe and the HTTP GET notification stream in MCP 2026-07-28?
note: One long-lived request whose response stream carries opted-in notifications.

q: What must be the first message a server sends on a new MCP subscription stream?
note: notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged, carrying the honored filter subset, before any other notification for that subscription.

q: What value does io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId carry on notifications from a listen stream?
note: It is the JSON-RPC id of the originating subscriptions/listen request — used to demultiplex on stdio.

q: Name the HTTP headers that every MCP Streamable HTTP POST request must include to mirror the JSON-RPC body for intermediaries.
note: Plus Mcp-Name on tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get.

q: When a tool parameter is annotated with x-mcp-header: "Region", what HTTP header name does the client send its value under?
note: x-mcp-header builds Mcp-Param-{name}; clients MUST support it, and invalid annotations exclude the tool from tools/list.

q: How does an MCP client carry a non-ASCII value in an Mcp-Param or Mcp-Name header?
note: The sentinel format =?base64?...?= of the UTF-8 bytes, lowercase markers.

q: How does an MCP client cancel an in-flight request on the Streamable HTTP transport in 2026-07-28?
note: Closing the SSE response stream IS the cancellation signal; notifications/cancelled is stdio-only.

q: Which three MCP features were deprecated together in revision 2026-07-28?
note: SEP-2577: remain functional in the window, but new implementations should not add them.

q: With the MCP Logging feature deprecated, how is per-request log level requested, and where should stdio servers log instead?
note: io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel in _meta; never emit notifications/message for requests without it.

q: Which two fields must list-type MCP results such as tools/list carry to support client caching, per the CacheableResult interface?
note: ttlMs freshness hint; cacheScope public/private for shared intermediaries.

q: Which RPC must every MCP 2026-07-28 server implement so clients can learn its supported protocol versions and capabilities up front?
note: Also the backward-compatibility probe on stdio.

q: What must an MCP client do when an SSE response stream breaks mid-request, given that Last-Event-ID resumability was removed?
note: The in-flight request is lost; re-issue as a new request with a new request id.

q: What replaced OAuth Dynamic Client Registration as the preferred MCP client registration mechanism in 2026-07-28?
note: RFC 7591 DCR is deprecated but kept for authorization servers without metadata-document support.

q: When an MCP client retries a request after an input_required result, may it reuse the original JSON-RPC id?
note: The retry is an independent request and MUST use a different id.

q: How does an MCP tool report a business-logic or API failure, as opposed to a protocol error like an unknown tool name?
note: Execution errors are a successful JSON-RPC result with isError:true, so the model can self-correct; protocol errors are JSON-RPC errors.

q: In MCP 2026-07-28, what JSON types may a tool's structuredContent field hold, and what changed from earlier revisions?
note: Widened from object-only to any JSON value conforming to outputSchema.

q: Why should an MCP server return tools from tools/list in a deterministic order?
note: Enables client-side caching and improves LLM prompt cache hit rates.

q: An MCP tools/list result must not vary per connection in 2026-07-28. What is the one input it MAY legitimately vary by, and why is that not connection state?
note: MUST NOT vary per-connection (no sessions) but MAY vary by authorization, which is per-request input.

q: What is the recommended inputSchema for an MCP tool that takes no parameters, and may inputSchema be null?
note: {type:object, additionalProperties:false}; inputSchema MUST NOT be null.

q: How must an MCP client treat the annotations on a tool definition when deciding whether to auto-approve a call?
note: Annotations are server assertions, untrusted unless from a trusted server.

q: Give the example the MCP spec uses for why a single resources/read may return several entries in its contents array.
note: A directory resource may return the contents of several files; clients must not assume one-to-one.

q: Which two mutually exclusive fields carry the payload of an MCP resource contents entry, and which one is base64?
note: text for textual data, blob for base64-encoded binary.

q: Which MCP method lists parameterized resource templates, and which field holds the RFC 6570 template string?
note: Not resources/list/templates; the field is uriTemplate, not uri.

q: What are the two valid values of the role field on an MCP PromptMessage?
note: Only user and assistant; there is no system role in prompt messages.

q: What structurally distinguishes a resource_link content block from an embedded resource content block in MCP?
note: resource_link puts uri/name/mimeType on the block itself; embedded resource nests them in a resource object.

q: In MCP pagination, what exactly signals that there are no more results, and how must a client treat an empty-string cursor?
note: An empty string is a VALID cursor; only a missing nextCursor ends the walk.

q: How many suggestion values may an MCP completion/complete result return at most, and which field says more exist?
note: Capped at 100 values; hasMore plus optional total report overflow.

q: What may an MCP stdio server write to stdout, and where should its debug logging go?
note: stdout carries ONLY valid MCP messages, one per line, no embedded newlines; logging goes to stderr.

q: What are an MCP client's three permitted options for handling a stdio server's stderr output, and what must it not infer from that output?
note: Clients MAY capture, forward, or ignore it, and SHOULD NOT assume stderr output indicates an error condition.

q: How does an MCP client cancel an in-flight request on the stdio transport, and why does it differ from Streamable HTTP?
note: stdio has one shared channel and no per-request stream to close.

q: Which field of an MCP DiscoverResult lists the protocol versions the server supports?
note: Client picks one for subsequent requests.

q: Which object of an MCP DiscoverResult holds serverInfo, and what three purposes is it intended for given that it is unverified?
note: Under _meta, self-reported and unverified — for display, logging and debugging, never for security decisions.

q: How often must an MCP client send the Authorization Bearer header to an HTTP MCP server, and which part of the URL must never carry the token?
note: Every request; tokens MUST NOT be in the URI query string, which leaks into logs and history.

q: What must an MCP server verify about an access token before processing a request, and what is the name of the forbidden practice of reusing that token against an upstream API?
note: Must be the intended audience per RFC 8707; token passthrough is forbidden — upstream needs its own token.

q: Which HTTP status and WWW-Authenticate error does an MCP server return when a valid token lacks the scope for an operation?
note: 403 + insufficient_scope, distinct from 401 for missing/invalid auth.

q: When an MCP client performs step-up authorization after an insufficient_scope error, which scopes must it request?
note: The union of previously requested scopes and the challenge scopes; servers need not echo already-granted scopes.

q: Which OAuth parameter must an MCP client include in both authorization and token requests to name the MCP server the token is for?
note: RFC 8707 Resource Indicators, using the server's canonical URI.

q: What must an MCP client do if an authorization server's metadata omits code_challenge_methods_supported?
note: Absence means no PKCE support; clients MUST refuse to proceed.

q: What must an MCP client ensure about the client_id value inside a Client ID Metadata Document it hosts?
note: The client_id inside must exactly match the document URL, so the identity is self-describing.

q: What resultType does an MCP server return to hand back an asynchronous task handle instead of blocking, under the tasks extension?
note: CreateTaskResult with resultType "task", carrying taskId, ttlMs and pollIntervalMs.

q: Which methods does the MCP tasks extension define for polling a task and for submitting requested input, and which older method was removed?
note: Polling via tasks/get replaced the blocking tasks/result; tasks/list was removed.

q: What must an MCP server check before answering a request with a CreateTaskResult, and where does it find that information?
note: The client must have declared io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks in the request's clientCapabilities extensions.

q: What is the extension identifier for MCP Apps, and which MIME type does a client declare to receive app payloads?
note: The identifier says ui, not apps — a common source of wrong capability keys.

q: What naming convention must a third-party MCP extension identifier follow?
note: Reverse-DNS vendor prefix the author owns, e.g. com.example/my-extension; prefix is mandatory.

q: In the MCP architecture, which component retains the full conversation history and enforces the isolation boundary between servers?
note: Servers see neither the whole conversation nor into other servers; the host holds it.
